scenario: A software-ecosystem study examines only open-source libraries still receiving downloads after maintainer-burnout attrition, recording mean weekly downloads of 48k (σ=10k). The active-use threshold is 30k downloads per week. The true mean downloads across all libraries at launch is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming weekly downloads is normally distributed with σ=10 k downloads, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>30]=48. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The open-source libraries still in active use weekly downloads set is a truncated-normal sample above the 30 threshold. Solving E[X|X>30]=μ+σφ((30−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((30−μ)/σ)=48 gives μ≈47.019. Only 95.6% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.9810 k downloads.

naive_answer: The true mean weekly downloads is 48 k downloads because that is the observed average among open-source libraries still in active use.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=30. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=48. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈47.019. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((30−47.019)/σ)≈0.95561.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 48,10,30
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-47.019)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.95561)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
